clue.text: Regularly praises good performance by exam candidate

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word praises, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A teacher's warm words for a student who did well in a test.
explanation.definitionFit: Achieving the required standard in an examination is called a pass, the result a candidate hopes for.

clue.text: Two men adopting name of a literary quartet?

parts.note: Alex is a man's name

indicators.note: adopting means the second man's name takes in the abbreviation for name

parts.note: Adrian is another man's name

explanation.surface: A pair of men taking on the title of some four-part literary work.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence Durrell's novels The Alexandria Quartet are set in the Egyptian city; the question mark flags the adjective as a sly definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Durrell's tetralogy is The Alexandria Quartet, so something belonging to that sequence of four novels is Alexandrian.

clue.text: Boys squashing fly in tiny bits

indicators.note: squashing pictures the boys pressing around the fly, enclosing it

parts.note: sons are boys
a midge is a small fly

explanation.surface: Lads crushing an insect into small fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a very small amount, so tiny bits are smidgeons, plural matching plural.

clue.text: Yours truly's funny idea: opening big gala?

parts.note: yours truly is the setter, giving me; the 's stands for has

indicators.note: funny suggests the letters of idea are made strange, rearranged

parts.note: a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of a comic notion for launching a grand celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yours truly' is crossword shorthand for the setter; 'funny' scrambles IDEA into DIAE, the middle of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged occasion designed to attract press coverage is a media event, which a big gala is likely to be.

clue.text: Very eager to mourn after old lady died

indicators.note: after places the word for mourning behind the mother and died

parts.note: old lady is informal for mother, ma
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
to keen is to wail in grief, to mourn

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious to grieve following the death of an elderly woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad keen is a British colloquial idiom for extremely enthusiastic, very eager to do something.

clue.text: Head of organisation re-recording late broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio chief's late-night repeat goes out over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A director-general is the title of the chief executive of some bodies, such as the BBC, so the head of an organisation.

clue.text: A driver initially stuck in French town hasn't succeeded in moving steadily

indicators.note: stuck in means that letter is lodged inside the shortened town name
hasn't means the town name goes without that letter

parts.note: Nantes is a city in western France
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of driver

explanation.surface: A motorist caught in a French town drives slowly because things are not going well.
explanation.walkthrough: Nantes without S gives NANTE; the D from 'driver initially' goes inside it, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a musical tempo marking meaning at a moderate walking pace, so moving steadily.

clue.text: Cook wants oven temperature set to top

indicators.note: set to top means the temperature letter is placed at the front, the top in a down answer

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops, a kind of oven

explanation.surface: A chef needs the oven heat turned up to the maximum.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a hop kiln, familiar in Kent as a round-roofed oast house.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast is to cook bread or similar by browning it under direct heat, a verb sense of cook.

clue.text: Confused writer about to retire?

indicators.note: to here means the writer and the word for about are taken to bed, put inside it

parts.note: to retire for the night is to go to bed
Oscar Wilde was an Irish playwright and wit
re is a short word meaning about, concerning

explanation.surface: An addled author on the point of giving up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to retire' reads as one phrase, an author nearing retirement; split it so 'about' is a piece and 'to' sends writer and piece into bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewildered is a direct synonym of confused, both meaning thoroughly puzzled.

clue.text: Parking area is restricted in much-visited city

indicators.note: restricted means the word is is confined between the other two letters

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Parking space is limited in a city full of tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city with the Leaning Tower draws vast numbers of tourists, a much-visited place.

clue.text: Line in funny story, say, about flock of birds

parts.note: a gag is a joke, a funny story

indicators.note: in places the line letter inside the turned abbreviation
about means the abbreviation for say is turned round

parts.note: eg is short for exempli gratia, for example, signalled by say

explanation.surface: A comedian slips a line into a joke about a group of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the usual signal for an example; 'about' turns it to GE, and 'in' lodges the line letter inside, giving GLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaggle is the collective noun for a flock of geese, especially on the ground.

clue.text: Arrangement to commit murder using four spades, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a hired killing is a deal struck with a hitman, a murder arrangement
in bridge the bid a side undertakes to make, such as four spades, has the same name

explanation.surface: A hit is arranged over a hand of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge, the final bid sets the number of tricks the declarer must win.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a binding agreement, including one taken out on someone's life, and also the bid to be made in bridge.

clue.text: Bar in Spain? So, it's a place to get drunk

indicators.note: to get drunk suggests the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Spanish pub, it is suggested, is somewhere to go drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub, but it is a bar of soap; Castile is a region of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Castile soap is a fine olive-oil soap from the Spanish region, sold in bars, hence a bar in Spain.

clue.text: Rejected unusual oriental edible root

indicators.note: rejected means the words for unusual and oriental together are thrown back, read backwards

parts.note: odd means unusual
E is the abbreviation for east, so oriental

explanation.surface: An odd Eastern root vegetable is turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns ODD plus E round as a whole, giving the root.
explanation.definitionFit: The eddo is the edible corm of the taro plant, a starchy tropical root vegetable.

clue.text: As movie artist, one is alert for remake

indicators.note: for remake means these letters are to be made again in a new order, like a film remake

explanation.surface: A film director says one stays watchful when reshooting a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Neorealism was the postwar Italian film movement of directors such as De Sica and Rossellini.
explanation.definitionFit: A neo-realist is a film-maker of the Italian neorealist school, so an artist working in movies.

clue.text: Cheese with chopped fruit topping for snack

indicators.note: topping for places the shortened fruit above the snack in this down answer
chopped means the fruit has its final letter cut off

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
a burger is a quick snack

explanation.surface: A cheese served with sliced fruit as a garnish for a light meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Limburger is a strong-smelling soft cheese originating in the Limburg region of Belgium and the Netherlands.

clue.text: Cockney's expressed desire for drink with little alcohol early in the day

indicators.note: a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, says the th sound as f, so the word for desire comes out differently

parts.note: thirst is the desire for a drink
light beer or lager has little alcohol

explanation.surface: A Londoner says he fancies a weak pint at the start of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech turns TH to F (thing becomes fing), so THIRST is heard as FIRST.
explanation.definitionFit: First light is dawn, when daylight first appears, so it means early in the day.

clue.text: Threatening look of the French pilgrims' destination

parts.note: to lour is to scowl, and a lour is a threatening look
des is French for of the, plural

explanation.surface: Glowering looks from French pilgrims on their way to a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lourdes in south-west France is a famous Catholic shrine where millions of pilgrims travel.

clue.text: Less sober foreign character must be brought into line

indicators.note: must be brought into means the character goes inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row or line
psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a foreign character

explanation.surface: A rather drunk foreigner has to be made to fall into line.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsier is the comparative of tipsy, slightly drunk, so less sober.

clue.text: Male needing help might employ her?

definitions.text: Male needing help might employ her?

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A man who needs assistance around the house might take on a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is a female domestic servant, someone a man needing help at home might hire.

clue.text: Industrious creature, tailless lizard from the West Indies

parts.note: the ant is proverbially hard-working

indicators.note: tailless means the lizard loses its final letter

parts.note: an iguana is a large tropical lizard

explanation.surface: A hard-working insect and a lizard missing its tail, both Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiguan describes someone or something from Antigua, an island in the Caribbean West Indies.

clue.text: Move swiftly, making a right din

parts.note: a row is a loud noise, a din

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off, kicking up quite a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrow is to move fast and straight like an arrow in flight, so to move swiftly.

clue.text: Archaic language used in Britain, once

indicators.note: used in signals the answer is contained within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An old tongue once spoken in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Taino was the language of the indigenous people of the Caribbean, now extinct; it has nothing to do with Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Taino is an extinct Arawakan language of the Caribbean, so an archaic one no longer spoken.

clue.text: One having pet pigeon

definitions.meaning: to be in a pet is to sulk, so one in a pet is someone who sulks with pushed-out lips
a breed of domestic pigeon able to inflate its crop

explanation.surface: A person keeping a bird as a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' here is an old word for a fit of sulking, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sulks, or pouts, and also a breed of pigeon with a puffed-up crop.

clue.text: Fleet deprived of power in surprise attack

indicators.note: deprived of means the word loses the letter for power

parts.note: fleet as an adjective means rapid

explanation.surface: A navy without engines is ambushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like a navy, but it is the adjective meaning fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden surprise attack on an enemy or a place.

clue.text: Barrie's family takes to northern town

parts.note: in J M Barrie's Peter Pan the children Wendy, John and Michael belong to the Darling family
taken as written

explanation.surface: The household in Barrie's play moves to the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Darlington is a town in County Durham, north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Darlington is a market town in County Durham, north-east England.

clue.text: Merchant seaman confronted by awkward situation, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak means the words are said aloud and spelt as they sound

parts.note: a sailor is a seaman, and a hole is an awkward situation; the hole is placed in front of the sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor finds himself in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLE plus SAILOR said aloud gives the trade word for a bulk merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesaler is a merchant who buys goods in bulk and sells them on to retailers.

clue.text: Guy in Hitchcock film

definitions.meaning: a guy is a ... used to steady a tent or mast
the 1948 Hitchcock thriller filmed in apparent single takes

explanation.definitionFit: A guy line is a cord, and Rope is the 1948 Alfred Hitchcock film starring James Stewart.
